transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-07-08 | Start: 09:00am PDT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Nightingale - Head of ML), Amita Rao (Nightingale - Eng Lead), Noah Fisher (Nightingale CTO)
Links shared (chat): pilot-pricing-v2.pdf, s3://redwood/pilot-results.csv, security-pack-link (redwood-security.pdf)
Summary: Short QBR/check-in focused on service runway, model governance, pilot scope for production rollout, and outstanding compliance items.
Topics: recent usage anomalies, latency vs cost tradeoffs, dedicated capacity pilot, SSO/SAML and SOC2 questions, benchmark plan.
Action items captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick check-in first 15 minutes on usage and then hands-on on pilot scope. Priya and I will cover the technical bits.
[00:28] Liam: Morning. Quick note — traffic spiked last week, we saw about a 2.6x jump on inference calls, mostly 1.5k token chat requests around peak. Not sure if that was client-side flaring or test harness.
[00:46] Priya: yeah, we pulled traces — looks like KV cache misses spiked, maybe because sequences increased. There's a small bug in your prefix handling that increases sequence length, that hurts batching.
[01:12] Amita: hm, we pushed a change to long-context mode the day before, could be related. Also we did increase sampling for analytics.
[01:30] Jordan: Perfect context. Two threads: runway (capacity + cost) and governance (model pinning, rollout rules). On runway, Noah, you mentioned wanting predictable latency under load?
[01:48] Noah: yes, we need p95 < 350ms for short chat flows, and p95 < 900ms for long form generation. Cost target is net token cost down 20% vs current hosted baseline.
[02:11] Priya: okay p95 numbers are doable with dedicated pools and some KV + batching tuning. But there's a tradeoff — dedicated committed capacity raises fixed monthly cost. We can show a blended unit cost model.
[02:33] Liam: can you quantify that? last month we paid for hosted model X and spikes burned a bunch. We'd like a model to decide when to fall back to lower-cost variants.
[02:51] Jordan: We'll send a micro-simulation — mix of dedicated baseline + burst to hosted. It models cost per 1M tokens at different tail latencies.
[03:12] Amita: also curious about quantization — we trialed 4-bit on local tests, quality seemed fine for embeddings but jittery for chat. Any guidance?
[03:34] Priya: Quantization depends on model family. For your retrieval-plus-chat flow we recommend mixed strategy: embed model quantized, chat model 8-bit or float16 for canopy of quality. We can supply quality regression plots.
[03:58] Noah: SOC 2 and KMS — your security pack is good but we need an answer: can you integrate with our HSM for key wrapping, and does audit logging capture token-level request hashes?
[04:20] Jordan: Short answer yes on KMS/HSM via customer-managed KMS; audit logs include token-level meta but not raw text by default. We'll share the security doc.
[04:43] Amita: what about SAML SSO? we need SCIM and RBAC syncing.
[05:01] Priya: Redwood supports SAML + SCIM; we sometimes see docs call it SAMMEL in transcriptions, haha. We'll need IdP metadata from you and can provision roles via SCIM.
[05:22] Liam: timeline question — we'd like a pilot with dedicated capacity for two weeks in staging, then a production rollout in 8 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:38] Jordan: Yes, a two-week dedicated pilot is our standard. Typical steps: pilot onboarding, run latency/quality benchmarks, iterate, then commit capacity. We'll outline gates.
[06:02] Priya: For the pilot we'll need a representative prompt set and a test harness. Send us the deck and the CSV you want measured against. We can run a 1-hour stress benchmark to capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
[06:25] Jordan: Note — bring-your-own-data privacy: we'll enable customer-only logs in the pilot for compliance.
[06:41] Noah: Good. Also competitor question — we compared Redwood to MegaCloud AI and FastServe.ai. Their latency was comparable but their pricing model was opaque. We liked Redwood's telemetry.
[07:00] Amita: on telemetry — can we get token-level cost breakdown per route?
[07:16] Priya: yes, token-level and route-level breakdowns in console. There may be small attribution diffs at very high throughput but we've got tracing hooks.
[07:34] Liam: any gotchas for on-prem or VPC? we have a couple of regulated clients that demand data residency.
[07:50] Jordan: Redwood Private (we also sometimes say Redwood Privet in notes) supports VPC and on-prem; the control plane can be customer-managed. We'll attach the private deployment checklist.
[08:08] Noah: Cool. Let's zoom into model governance — we want canary rollouts, automatic rollback on quality regressions, and a way to pin model versions to routes.
[08:29] Priya: we support per-route pinning, and rollouts can be configured as canary percent + auto fallback to previous stable model if quality drop detected against an eval set.
[08:49] Amita: how are regressions measured? do you integrate with our eval suite?
[09:05] Priya: yep you can push eval sets and define thresholds. We also have built-in prompts or you can use Redwood Evals. Alerts can be routed to Slack or PagerDuty.
[09:25] Liam: would Redwood automatically revert on latency SLO breach? sometimes that happens independent of quality.
[09:44] Jordan: You can set rollout policies by latency SLOs too — e.g., roll forward only if p95 < threshold. Fallback to cheaper model is possible.
[10:04] (brief crosstalk) Noah: ok, show me cost math — committed capacity month vs burst.
[10:20] Jordan: (shares screen) Here's a sim: committed 4 A100 equiv nodes for baseline at $X/month yields unit cost Y; bursts use hosted at per-token. There's a break-even at roughly 3.8M tokens/day.
[10:45] Amita: got it. We need that in a spreadsheet we can plug our actual daily usage into.
[11:01] Jordan: we'll send the model along with a worked example using your July spike as a scenario.
[11:19] Priya: back to technical — we noticed manual flushing of KV cache in your app which actually causes more misses; if you change to prefix-preserve mode you'll see fewer misses and better batching.
[11:40] Amita: that's from our prefetch logic; we'll change it and retest.
[11:52] Liam: another practical: how do you handle throttling and rate-limit headers? We want graceful degradation that surfaces to users.
[12:08] Priya: we return standard retry-after and also a route-level fallback you can configure. There's also built-in prioritization for important routes.
[12:26] Noah: security follow-up: are logs immutable and do you support customer-managed log forwarding to our S3?
[12:40] Jordan: yes — logs can be delivered to your S3 with encryption-at-rest and keys managed by your KMS. Audit logs are write-once in the control plane.
[12:58] (silence, typing sounds)
[13:18] Jordan: quick check — can we commit to the two-week pilot next week?
[13:32] Noah: Yes, assuming pricing is acceptable. Also we need a clear exit criteria and a rollback plan.
[13:45] Jordan: we'll include exit criteria: p95 latency target, throughput target, and quality thresholds on eval set. Rollback plan will be documented.
[14:02] Priya: For benchmarks, give us 1 representative heavy prompt, 3 medium, 5 short; we'll run both single-stream and concurrent throughput. Results in CSV.
[14:22] Amita: noted. We'll prep the harness.
[14:36] Liam: any architectural notes for production — autoscale granularity and cold start behavior?
[14:50] Priya: autoscale is configured by queue depth and token-per-second; cold starts are sub-second for warm pool but for cold containers there can be a few seconds. We recommend warm pools for latency-sensitive routes.
[15:12] Noah: can we simulate autoscale cost? sometimes spikes trigger many nodes.
[15:27] Jordan: yes the sim will include autoscale policies with cost curves. We'll show worst-case and amortized cost.
[15:44] (brief hold while Jordan scrolls)
[16:05] Priya: small note — your eval showed a 0.6% semantic drift on the fallback model at 4-bit; we'll annotate examples where it failed.
[16:21] Amita: thanks, that's useful.
[16:36] Liam: org question — who will own this pilot internally at Nightingale?
[16:49] Noah: I'll be sponsor; Amita will run engineering, Liam will own ML metrics.
[17:03] Jordan: great. We'll treat that as the RACI.
[17:20] (typing)
[17:40] Jordan: Recap & next steps: 1) Jordan send pilot pricing + worked spreadsheet (due 7/12). 2) Priya run the 1-hour latency/throughput benchmark with your harness (due 7/11). 3) Noah share SAML IdP metadata + compliance contact (due 7/10). 4) Customer to provide prompt set and test deck (due 7/11). Any objections?
[18:04] Noah: none.
[18:14] Amita: one more: can we get a short runbook for incident playbooks tied to rollouts?
[18:28] Priya: yes we'll attach a runbook and a rollback checklist.
[18:40] Liam: thanks. How soon can we see the security pack with HSM details?
[18:52] Jordan: by EOD tomorrow we'll share the redwood-security.pdf link and KMS integration doc.
[19:04] (brief informal talk)
[19:28] Jordan: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the CRM.
[19:36] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional proper nouns misheard (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicate in notes), SAMMEL -> SAML, KV cache sometimes spelled K V cache. There may be partial overlaps in speaker labels where Fireflies misaligned audio.

Attachments referenced in chat: pilot-pricing-v2.pdf, s3://redwood/pilot-results.csv, redwood-security.pdf

End of transcript.
